failure_modes.name: confident_but_wrong
failure_modes.what_it_means: The model was sure and wrong. The failure a reviewer would not think to check, and the one that most needs the confidence signal to mean something.

failure_modes.name: abstention_would_have_been_better
failure_modes.what_it_means: The model was already unsure and answered anyway. Abstaining would have cost coverage and saved an error, which is the trade the routing threshold exists to make.

failure_modes.name: rules_right_model_wrong
failure_modes.what_it_means: The deterministic baseline got these and the model did not. Every row here is an argument for the hybrid, and against replacing the rules with the model.

failure_modes.name: model_right_rules_wrong
failure_modes.what_it_means: What the model is actually buying: rows the baseline could not answer or answered wrongly. Counted over correct model rows, not failures.

failure_modes.name: thin_description
failure_modes.what_it_means: Wrong on rows whose description is under 15 characters. Not a prompt problem: the row does not carry enough to decide, and a better prompt cannot add context that is absent.

failure_modes.name: polysemous_merchant
failure_modes.what_it_means: Wrong on a merchant that carries more than one gold label in this dataset. Genuinely two things; no description-only system resolves these reliably.

failure_modes.name: annotators_disagreed_too
failure_modes.what_it_means: Wrong on rows where the two human annotators also disagreed. The model is failing where people find it hard, which bounds how much of this is fixable by prompting.

failure_modes.name: abstained
failure_modes.what_it_means: Declined to answer. Not an error, but it is lost coverage and it belongs in the same picture.

note: Counts and taxonomy label pairs only. No merchant, amount, date, or transaction appears here or can be recovered from it.
